description: Article format templates for structural variety. The Analyst picks the format based on topic, intent, and what was used recently. Never use the same format for 3+ articles in a row.

practitioner-story.name: Practitioner Story
practitioner-story.description: Lead with a real scenario or experience, then expand into analysis. The story IS the hook and the structure.
best_for: tool reviews where hands-on experience matters
structure: Open with a specific practitioner scenario (the problem, the numbers, the outcome)
What we learned / what went wrong
The broader context (how this applies to others)
Technical deep-dive on the key decision points
What we'd do differently
Takeaway (1-2 sentences, no summary block)
practitioner-story.tone_notes: Most personal. Heavy on 'we' and 'I'. Specific dollar amounts and dates throughout.

analysis-piece.name: Analysis / Deep Dive
analysis-piece.description: Structured examination of a topic with clear sections. The standard review format, but sections should NOT all follow the same pattern.
structure: Hook: concrete claim or surprising fact (2-3 sentences)
Context: where this fits in the market (short)
3-5 analytical sections (VARY structure: some data-led, some anecdote-led, some opinion-led)
Honest assessment of limitations
When to use / when not to use
Optional: FAQ only if DataForSEO returns real PAA questions with volume
analysis-piece.tone_notes: Balanced but opinionated. Lead sections with the most interesting point, not background.

contrarian-take.name: Contrarian / Hot Take
contrarian-take.description: Lead with an opinion that challenges conventional wisdom. Back it up with evidence. This format stands out in a sea of neutral AI coverage.
best_for: topics where the consensus is wrong or oversimplified
structure: Open with the contrarian claim (bold, specific, no hedging)
Why most people get this wrong
The evidence (data, experience, specific examples)
The strongest counter-argument (steelman it honestly)
Where the nuance lives
What to actually do about it
contrarian-take.tone_notes: Strongest voice. More 'I' statements. Take a clear position and defend it.

comparison.name: Head-to-Head Comparison
comparison.description: Compare 2-3 options with asymmetric coverage. Spend more words on what matters more. NOT a balanced pro/con for each.
structure: Why this comparison matters right now (not a generic intro)
The criteria that actually matter (3-4, not 10)
Asymmetric comparison sections: go deep on differentiators, skip what's similar
Pricing reality check (table or inline, not both)
The verdict: specific recommendations by use case
Optional: FAQ if DataForSEO returns real PAA
comparison.tone_notes: Decision-oriented. Reader should know what to pick by the end.

how-it-works.name: How It Works / Tutorial
how-it-works.description: Teach something practical. Show, don't just tell. Code examples, CLI commands, real configurations.
structure: What you'll be able to do after reading this (specific outcome, not vague promise)
Prerequisites (keep short — 2-3 bullets max)
The walkthrough (numbered steps with real code/commands)
What to watch out for (gotchas from experience)
Next steps (what to build on top of this)
how-it-works.tone_notes: Most practical. Heavy on code blocks and specific commands. Fewer opinions, more 'here's exactly how'.
